name: check

description: After reading a source that a memory cites (a file, page, paper), say what you found: `ok` (as cited), `changed` or `missing`. The daemon never reads sources itself. Side effect: the report is stored; `changed` and `missing` open a review task for each memory that cites it. The memories themselves are not changed.

request.description:
Report what you found when you went back to a source: `ok` (as cited), `changed` (the
cited statement may no longer hold) or `missing`. `changed` and `missing` open a review task
for each memory that cites it.

name: check_source

description: Take a pending task so others do not. Side effect: the task is marked claimed by you.
name: claim_task

description: Finish a claimed task. Resolve it first with an ordinary proposal (`remember`: supersede the duplicates), then complete with decision `merge` or `supersede` and that proposal's id; `distinct` says the memories differ (not raised again); `defer` parks it. Side effect: the task is closed.

result.description:
How a maintenance task was resolved. `merge` (a duplicate cluster), `supersede` (an
update), `retract` and `revise` (a memory reported wrong or expiring) must cite the proposal
that did it; `distinct` (two memories differ) and `keep` (the memory stands) are remembered and
not raised again; `defer` parks the task for later.

name: complete_task

description: Investigation only: a concept's earlier versions (label, aliases, definition, status), the relations it has had including ended ones, and the ontology changes that touched it. Ordinary tools never show these.
name: concept_history

description: Find concepts by label or alias (`python`, `ssh`) to get the ids that `about`, anchors and qualifiers refer to, with their relations. Empty: no such concept; propose one with `propose_ontology_change` rather than guessing an id.
name: concepts

description: Scan for duplicates and updates and queue each finding once as a task. Side effect: task records are created (and tasks whose memories changed are closed); no memory is changed.
name: detect_tasks

description: Say that a recalled memory was `helpful`, `applied`, `irrelevant`, `missed` (it should have come back), `outdated` or `wrong`. Give the `query` it came back for and, when shown, the recall `trace`. Side effect: the verdict is stored. `outdated` and `wrong` also queue a maintenance task for a human or agent to retract, revise or confirm the memory; the memory itself is not changed.
name: feedback

description: Read-only: your recorded feedback ranked by how likely it is to be a mistake (it disagrees with the ranking at recall time, a verdict flipped, or a burst from one source). Tell the user what looks wrong; vetoing is theirs to do (console or API).
name: feedback_outliers

description: Read-only scan for memories that say the same thing (clusters, oldest first) and for restatements with a changed value (updates). Nothing is changed: resolve a cluster with a `supersede` or `retract` proposal via `remember`.

description: Store, change or retire a memory by sending a proposal of ops. To store something new use op `add` (a `kind` and its `fields`; the schema lists them). `revise`, `supersede` and `retract` (and `link`, `annotate` in the full profile) act on memories that already exist: use ids from recall or an earlier result, never an invented one. The proposal is validated, then committed or held for review: say it is saved only when `status` is `committed` (`pending` means a human must approve). Read the findings: a duplicate warning usually means supersede; an unscoped warning means `revise` that memory, not add it again. Side effects: a proposal is recorded; if the policy commits it, memories are added or superseded or retracted (history is kept). Memories go to your own space; `space: global` writes to the shared memory and needs permission.

task.
